A.label: Agent-Assisted Human Commerce
A.description: The agent buys for a human using human payment rails. The human is the economic actor.

B.label: Agent-as-Workforce
B.description: The agent replaces a human worker. The enterprise is the economic actor.

Ccr.label: Autonomous A2A Commerce (Blockchain)
Ccr.description: The agent is the economic actor. Own wallet, own identity on-chain, transacts without human in the loop.

Cs.label: Autonomous A2A Commerce (Non-Crypto)
Cs.description: Agents transact autonomously without blockchain. Machine-native currency in a centralized double-entry ledger.

D.label: Analytical and Regulatory
D.description: They analyze what Categories A through C will do to markets, workers, and systemic stability.

E.label: Infrastructure and Standards
E.description: Horizontal layers: how agents find each other, verify identity, invoke tools, agree on terms.

definitions.definition: Assistant agents act on behalf of consumers and service agents represent businesses, interacting programmatically to facilitate transactions.
definitions.notes: arXiv:2505.15799. The most cited academic definition. Key concepts: "unscripted" vs. "unrestricted" interactions, "agentic walled gardens." Payment: fiat/abstracted. Identity: human OAuth. Disputes: platform intermediaries.

definitions.definition: Checkout flows where an AI agent discovers a product for a human and pays via Stripe's Shared Payment Token.
definitions.notes: agenticcommerce.dev. Deployed in ChatGPT as "Instant Checkout" with Etsy and Shopify merchants. Payment: Stripe SPT. Identity: delegated human. Disputes: chargeback.

definitions.definition: Full commerce lifecycle -- discovery, comparison, checkout, post-purchase -- with the agent navigating the journey for the human.
definitions.notes: A checkout state machine extending human e-commerce to agentic surfaces. Payment: processor agnostic. Identity: protocol negotiation. Disputes: e-commerce flows.

definitions.definition: OAuth-based payments allowing agents to purchase on behalf of their human owners using saved payment methods.
definitions.notes: Payment: Mastercard/PayPal/fiat. Identity: OAuth. Disputes: chargeback. The agent never touches money it doesn't have permission to spend.

definitions.definition: Agent-initiated payments via tokenization and biometric verification, tied back to human cardholders.
definitions.notes: Visa defending interchange revenue. The agent initiates, but biometric auth ensures a human is behind every transaction. Payment: fiat card networks. Identity: tokenization + biometric. Disputes: network rules.

definitions.definition: Agentic Tokens with spend limits set by the human, issued to AI agents via passkeys.
definitions.notes: Payment: fiat card networks. Identity: Agentic Tokens + passkeys. Disputes: network rules. The agent has a budget, not a bank account.

definitions.definition: Agents break the "consumer inertia dividend" -- profits derived from humans failing to optimize -- with real-time micro-auctions for best rates.
definitions.notes: Projects agent-mediated commerce at $3-5T by 2030. Payment: Open Banking / wallets. Identity: OAuth2/VTS. Disputes: unclear liability.

definitions.definition: AI agents act on behalf of consumers or businesses to research, negotiate and complete purchases.
definitions.notes: ibm.com/think. Straightforward Category A framing -- the agent shops, the human pays.

definitions.definition: AI agents embedded in CRM workflows to assist human buyers and sellers through existing sales processes.
definitions.notes: Enterprise-facing. The agent optimizes the sales funnel but the transaction is human-to-human.

definitions.definition: AI agents assisting financial advisors and clients with product discovery and transaction execution.
definitions.notes: Financial services context. Payment: traditional fiat. Identity: human-authenticated. Disputes: human/regulatory.

definitions.definition: AI-powered personalization agents for e-commerce, optimizing product recommendations and checkout for human shoppers.
definitions.notes: Payment: traditional fiat. Disputes: standard e-commerce. The agent is a conversion optimization tool.

definitions.definition: AI agents acting on our behalf -- shopping, negotiating, executing purchases.
definitions.notes: Distinguished from Deloitte's enterprise/workforce framing (see B4). Same firm, different reports, different categories.

definitions.definition: Agents need to transact with businesses and one another -- M2M payments on Visa/Stripe rails, fiat + stablecoins.
definitions.notes: Hybrid A/C. The closest Category A initiative to autonomous payment, but built on human financial infrastructure. Payment: Visa/Stripe. Identity: API key.

definitions.definition: Intents become interfaces, agents become default delegates, workflows become the product.
definitions.notes: Hybrid A/B. The agent replaces the app as the primary interface -- but the human remains the principal. Workflows, not transactions, are the unit of value.

definitions.definition: 100 million agents by 2028. 33% of enterprise apps will include agentic AI. 15% of day-to-day business decisions made autonomously. $18T in economic activity influenced.
definitions.notes: Also predicted 40% of agentic AI projects scrapped by 2027 (Reuters). The optimism and the skepticism come from the same analyst house.

definitions.definition: Agents will be commoditized and priced at compute costs due to near-infinite supply. Services shift from selling tools to selling results.
definitions.notes: The SaaS seat model dies. Outcome-based pricing replaces it. Payment: outcome-based. Identity: API key. Disputes: SLA.

definitions.definition: An agent economy is one in which agents don't just communicate information -- they transfer resources, make transactions, keep track of each other, understand trust and reliability, and actually have their own economy.
definitions.notes: AI Ascent keynote. Hybrid B/C. Three challenges: persistent identity, seamless communication protocols ("TCP/IP for agents"), security/trust.

definitions.definition: Agents as autonomous partners inside organizations, making multi-step decisions without human approval at each step.
definitions.notes: Distinguished from Deloitte's commerce framing (see A12). Here the agent is an employee, not a shopper.

definitions.definition: 1.7x ROI on AI operations. 21% of organizations running multi-agent systems.
definitions.notes: The numbers are real but the framing is enterprise-internal. Agents optimize existing processes, not create new markets.

definitions.definition: Agents divide responsibilities, coordinate tasks, cross-check each other's work inside enterprise workflows.
definitions.notes: Academic treatment of multi-agent coordination in enterprise settings.

definitions.definition: AI as entrepreneur -- businesses that operate with minimal human involvement.
definitions.notes: Pushes Category B toward its logical extreme. If the agent runs the business, is the enterprise still the economic actor? The boundary with Category C starts to blur.

definitions.definition: Vertical-specific agents as workers -- legal, medical, compliance. Outcome-based pricing per vertical.
definitions.notes: The agent is a specialist, not a generalist. Different verticals need different agents. The pricing model follows the vertical, not the compute.

definitions.definition: "Machine Economy" -- agents negotiate, trade, and deliver services using FET/ASI tokens with self-custodial wallets.
definitions.notes: The earliest mover. Active since 2021. Payment: FET/ASI tokens. Identity: blockchain wallets. fetch.ai.

definitions.definition: Agent economies where agents hire and sell services to each other, governed by on-chain DAO mechanisms.
definitions.notes: Payment: crypto/tokens. Identity: on-chain wallets. Disputes: DAO governance. olas.network.

definitions.definition: HTTP 402 status code + stablecoin micropayments. Account-less, subscription-free, pay-per-use.
definitions.notes: Settlement in <500ms. Payment: USDC. Identity: account-less crypto. Disputes: none. x402.org.

definitions.definition: Gas-free USDC transfers down to $0.000001. Off-chain aggregation, batched on-chain settlement.
definitions.notes: Eliminates gas fees by batching. Payment: USDC, zero-gas. Identity: EVM wallet.

definitions.definition: EVM-compatible Layer 1 specifically for agentic payments. "Know Your Agent" (KYA) framework with hierarchical on-chain identity.
definitions.notes: Payment: stablecoin, zero-gas. Identity: KYA / "Digital Agent Passport." Disputes: smart contract.

definitions.definition: Four-layer Machine Economy framework: infrastructure, identity, economic, governance. Settlement via crypto/x402.
definitions.notes: Payment: crypto/x402. Identity: ERC-8004. A VC framework, not a protocol -- but influential in shaping how the crypto ecosystem thinks about agent economics.

definitions.definition: Token economies incentivizing agent behavior. Virtuals, AI16z, and Token-of-Things as examples. Decentralized governance.
definitions.notes: Academic treatment of crypto-native agent economics. Payment: crypto/tokens. Identity: decentralized.

definitions.definition: Five-layer architecture: physical infrastructure (DePIN), identity (W3C DIDs), cognition (RAG + MCP), economic settlement (account abstraction), collective governance (DAOs).
definitions.notes: The most architecturally complete proposal in Category C. Agents as "sovereign economic peers." Payment: crypto. Identity: DIDs/wallets. Disputes: DAO.

definitions.definition: "Agentic Process Automation" -- autonomous businesses with DID-based identity and crypto/fiat settlement.
definitions.notes: Hybrid crypto/fiat but blockchain-first. Payment: crypto/fiat. Identity: DIDs.

definitions.definition: "Machine Economy" via IoT + distributed ledger technology. The historical precursor -- machines paying machines for data and services.
definitions.notes: Legacy project. Payment: IOTA tokens. Identity: ledger IDs. Predates the LLM wave by years. The concept was right; the AI wasn't ready.

definitions.definition: Natural language commands routed to DeFi across 60+ chains. MCP integration for agent-to-DeFi interaction.
definitions.notes: Payment: crypto/stablecoins. The agent speaks natural language; the infrastructure translates to on-chain transactions.

definitions.definition: Agents with own currency ($TCK), escrow-backed settlement, quantitative reputation (CRI 0-100), and automated dispute resolution. No blockchain.
definitions.notes: agenticeconomy.dev. Payment: TCK (machine-native, closed-loop). Identity: API key + JWT. Disputes: deterministic rules + competitive verification markets. Settlement neutrality: MCP, A2A, and REST converge on the same escrow pipeline. The only non-crypto entry in Category C.

definitions.definition: Three trust domains: human-to-human, human-to-agent, agent-to-agent. Trust is the fundamental constraint, not compute.
definitions.notes: Also converges on Know Your Agent (KYA) as a cross-category identity framework. The WEF does not build infrastructure, but it shapes the regulatory conversation.

definitions.definition: "Agentic Finance" -- the Agentic Financial Market Model (AFMM). Four-layer architecture: perception, reasoning, strategy, execution.
definitions.notes: Warns of algorithmic herding, automated bank runs, flash crashes. Engineering the "Finternet" -- interoperable network for programmable value systems.

definitions.definition: Agents as sovereign actors. AI-native banks. Agents that own assets, sign contracts, and execute trades independently.
definitions.notes: The VC framing that pushes Category C toward its most radical conclusion. Influential in shaping narrative, less in building infrastructure.

definitions.definition: If Category B agents replace enough workers, wages collapse, consumer demand collapses. If demand collapses, the businesses that agents transact with have nothing to sell.
definitions.notes: Convergent concern across multiple economic analyses. Suggests that non-extractive settlement designs may have structural advantages.

definitions.definition: Frames the agent economy through Crossmint, Olas, and on-chain rails. Mentions ACK-ID, Nevermined ID.
definitions.notes: Hybrid C/D. VC analysis that straddles building and analyzing. Primary framing is analytical.

definitions.definition: Machines negotiate, trade, and transact without human oversight.
definitions.notes: Consultancy framing. Category C aspirational language wrapped in Category D analysis.

definitions.definition: Trillions of AI agents as buyers, sellers, collaborators. NANDA building the "DNS of the agentic web."
definitions.notes: Visionary framing. The NANDA reference (agent naming/discovery) connects to Category E infrastructure.

definitions.definition: Agent discovery and communication. Agents publish Agent Cards at /.well-known/agent.json, exchange tasks via JSON-RPC over HTTPS.
definitions.notes: v0.3. 150+ partners. Does not specify payment or settlement. The discovery layer for agents -- but without economics.

definitions.definition: A standard for LLMs to discover and invoke external tools. Focused on tool interoperability.
definitions.notes: modelcontextprotocol.io. Does not specify payment, settlement, or reputation. The tool layer -- but without economics.

definitions.definition: "Digital Agent Passport" -- Know Your Agent identity verification for autonomous agents.
definitions.notes: The KYC equivalent for machines. Cross-category: any category that needs to verify an agent's identity can use it.

definitions.definition: Standard for terms and agreements between autonomous entities.
definitions.notes: The first formal standards body to address agent-to-agent contracts. Still in draft. If ratified, it becomes the legal infrastructure for Category C.

definitions.definition: SEO is for humans. ADO is for agents. A brand invisible to agents is invisible to the agentic economy.
definitions.notes: New concept. Implies that Category A and Category C will develop parallel discovery mechanisms.

definitions.definition: Cryptographic proof of work delivery for agent commerce. IETF standardization track.
definitions.notes: Hybrid C/E. Addresses the verification problem at the protocol level. Complementary to escrow-based approaches.

definitions.definition: Working paper on terminology and regulatory framing for agentic AI systems.
definitions.notes: Hybrid D/E. The OECD defines terms and shapes regulatory vocabulary. What they name, legislators regulate.

definitions.definition: The identity layer for the agent economy. Finding: non-human identities outnumber human employees 96-to-1 in finance.
definitions.notes: The 96:1 ratio is striking -- finance already has more machine identities than human ones. Keycard builds the credential layer.

definitions.definition: The complete integration and participation of economically autonomous acting machines in economic processes.
definitions.notes: The earliest academic paper to formalize machine economic participation. Three prerequisites: autonomy, connectivity, intelligence. Predates the protocol wave by four years.

definitions.definition: Verify-then-Pay Infrastructure for Trusted Agentic Commerce. Escrow + TEE/TLS verification.
definitions.notes: Hybrid C/E. Proves the seller delivered what the buyer paid for. Complementary to reputation systems.
